text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach on streaming-api in eu-west-1. p99 ~ 6.2s, p95 ~ 1.4s. Error rate slightly elevated. Auto-mitigation attempted (fallback -> cold-model) but not enough. Paging oncall.
ken: On it. Confirming scope — is this across all models or just a subset? Any recent deploys/rollouts?

maria: looks correlated with the prefix-hash v4 rollout we started 25m ago. I see cache hit-rate for prefix-cache down to 5-8% on the hot shards. Could be invalidation mismatch after the hash change.

alex: confirmed. Running prom queries now. Query I ran:

sum(rate(streaming_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

p99 = 6.2s, p95 = 1.37s. Also saw stream stall errors in pod logs:
"streaming: kv-cache miss for prefix key id=0x7f1a... fallback to disk, wait=3400ms"
repeated across many requests.

sophia: Customer impact: we have ~12 customers with active streaming sessions in eu-west-1; internal SLO page shows p99 breach for two Business customers (alerting). We should triage as SEV-2 until mitigated. Notifying CSMs.

ken: Ok plan: 1) pause prefix-hash v4 rollout 2) roll back servers to hash v3 3) enable aggressive warmup for the cache and increase prefetch window 4) if needed, route new streaming traffic to eu-west-2 fallback pool.

Who can run the rollback?

maria: I can do the config rollback. Two steps: flip the feature-flag in config-service and trigger cache warmup job for affected shards. Command to flip flag (prod):

curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
https://config.internal.redwood/api/flags/prefix_hash_rollout 
-d '{"state":"paused","target_version":"v3"}'

Afterwards run warmup job:

./bin/cache-warmup --shard <shard-id> --parallel 8 --prefetch-window 256

I'll run the flag flip now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config-update queued by maria. Change will hit config-plane in ~25s and controllers in ~2m. CI checks green.

alex: While that's happening, I recommend moving streaming traffic to the secondary routing pool as a containment. Quick patch for the router (k8s):

kubectl -n infra patch service/router --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/trafficPolicy","value":{"preferredPool":"eu-west-2"}}]'

This will start new sessions in eu-west-2 within ~30s. Existing sessions stay on current nodes.

ken: Good. Maria, confirm when flag flip completes so we can watch cache hit-rate. I'll keep oncall until it's stable. Sophia, keep CSMs updated with ETA 30m.

maria: Flag flipped. Config-plane show:

{
  "flag":"prefix_hash_rollout",
  "state":"paused",
  "target_version":"v3",
  "updated_by":"maria",
  "updated_at":"1713004389"
}

Warmup job launched for shards 3,4,7. Logs:

[warmup] shard=3 prefetch=0..255 hits=0/256 warmup_time=0.9s
[warmup] shard=4 prefetch=0..255 hits=12/256 warmup_time=1.2s

Initial hit-rate improving but still low on shard 7.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: router patch applied by alex. New sessions being preferred to eu-west-2.

alex: Seeing router propagation. New session rate to eu-west-2 ~70% now. Old sessions still on the impacted pods.

ken: Monitoring p99. prometheus query results after rollback/warmup (2m window): p99 = 1.1s, p95 = 0.9s. Looks much better. Anyone still seeing streaming stalls?

sophia: Customer-facing: I posted note to the two affected CSMs, they acknowledged. No escalations yet. We'll keep the SEV-2 until p99 stable for 15m.

maria: shard 7 hit-rate still lagging but improving (now ~35%). We should run an on-demand re-warm for hot keys; I'll enqueue targeted prefetch for top prefixes.

Command:
./bin/prefetch --shard 7 --prefixes-file top_prefixes_shard7.txt --concurrency 16

Running that now.

alex: Quick follow-up: we should add a transient fallback in the runtime so that large misses don't block streaming RPCs — short-circuit to serve partial output and continue warming in background. Filing a small change but won't be hotfixed right now.

Issue: https://redwood-internal/issue/INC-12345

ken: Agree, makes sense as postmortem action. For now we have p99 down to ~950ms. Let's maintain routing preference and monitor for 30m. If stable, we'll close the oncall handoff and create postmortem.

Action items:
- maria: complete targeted prefetch for shards 3/4/7 (in progress) [IN PROGRESS]
- alex: monitor router metrics & session migration [IN PROGRESS]
- sophia: update CSMs every 15m and prepare customer impact summary [IN PROGRESS]
- ken: lead live-triage and prepare handoff notes

Handoff ETA: I'll remain oncall until 1713008045 or until stability confirmed.

maria: prefetch finished. shard 7 hit-rate now 68%. No further streaming stall logs.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config-plane propagation complete across controllers at 1713004762.

ken: Good job team. p99 steady ~880ms over 10m, p95 ~720ms. Downgrading severity to SEV-3 and transitioning to post-incident ticketing.

I'll create the incident doc and assign postmortem to eng-runtime + eng-ml to investigate prefix-hash rollout gating and add extra prewarm steps in rollout runbooks.

sophia: Adding customer notes: affected customers list + session IDs, message sent to CSMs. No refunds requested so far.

alex: logging the quick router-change commands and rollback commands in the incident thread for ops runbook.

ken: Handoff to next oncall (sophia) at 1713008045. Please continue monitoring for 30m and escalate if p99 rises >1.5s.

Closing live triage. Postmortem ticket: https://redwood-internal/pm/INC-1713004321

sophia: acknowledged. I'll take post-triage monitoring. Thanks everyone :heart:

Note: This thread contains the root alert and all coordination. See runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/prefix-cache-rollouts for detailed rollback steps and postmortem template.
